_note: Owner: P4. Space biology facts from NASA OSDR (Open Science Data Repository). Each text only says what the study page itself says (checked 2026-11-15). Cards point here with factId. Do not invent facts.

facts.study: Targeting myostatin/activin A protects against skeletal muscle and bone loss during spaceflight
facts.text: Mice that spent 33 days on the Space Station lost muscle and bone. Scientists study this to protect astronauts on long trips.
Plants can feel which way is down. On the Space Station, scientists spun seedlings in a centrifuge to give them different gravity, from almost none up to Earth's.

facts.study: Microbiological and nutritional analysis of lettuce crops grown on the International Space Station-VEG01B
facts.text: Astronauts grew lettuce in the Veggie garden on the Space Station. Then it was sent back to Earth, where scientists checked its germs and nutrients.

facts.study: Microbial Observatory (ISS-MO): Study of BSL-2 bacterial isolates from the International Space Station
facts.text: Germs live on the Space Station too. Scientists collected some of them, and many could resist several germ-fighting medicines (antibiotics).

facts.study: Light has a principal role in the Arabidopsis transcriptomic response to the spaceflight environment
facts.text: Small plants grew on the Space Station in the light and in the dark. Their leaves reacted to space more than their root tips, and light made a big difference.

facts.study: Gene-metabolite networks associated with impediment of bone fracture repair in spaceflight
facts.text: Space can make it harder for broken bones to heal. Mice with a small bone injury lived on the Space Station for about 4 weeks so scientists could study it.

facts.study: Artificial Gravity Attenuates the Transcriptomic Response to Spaceflight in the Optic Nerve and Retina -- Retina data
facts.text: Weightlessness can stress the eyes. When mice on the Space Station were spun to make artificial gravity, their eyes changed less.

facts.study: Microgravity effects on leaf morphology, cell structure, carbon metabolism and mRNA expression of dwarf wheat
facts.text: In 2002, dwarf wheat grew in space for 73 days, and the crew harvested it 7 times.

facts.study: Gene expression profiling for spaceflight induced-neuroinflammation in the mouse brain
facts.text: Mice spent 35 days on the Space Station. Back on Earth, 54 genes in their brains worked differently, many of them linked to stress and inflammation.

facts.study: SpaceX Inspiration4 PBMC Profiling: snRNA-seq, snATAC-seq, and T-cell and B-cell repertoire profiling
facts.text: In 2021, four private astronauts flew around Earth for 3 days. They gave blood before and after the flight so scientists could study their immune cells.

facts.study: Low dose (0.04 Gy) irradiation (LDR) and hindlimb unloading (HLU) microgravity in mice: brain transcriptomic and epigenomic data
facts.text: Space dangers can be tested on Earth too. For 21 days, mice got a small dose of radiation while their back legs were lifted off the ground to copy weightlessness.
